page: Microsoft Azure E8ns_v6 is an Env6 family virtual machine configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server features 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for matrix mathematics, and cryptographic acceleration via VAES and SHA_NI. The instance operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and does not include local storage or built-in GPUs, though it is designated as Premium Storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the E8ns_v6 demonstrates balanced performance characteristics. Its single-core capabilities are notable, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2040.0 and a text processing score of 2501.0, both placing in the strong top 25% tier. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 7845.77 and a Passmark CPU score of 14017.42, both falling within the average range. Memory bandwidth tests show 608.18 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 61.47 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. For workload execution, the server achieves 10.8 million operations per second on Redis SET operations and 14.36 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. A key performance tradeoff is observed in large-model language processing; while text generation for a small 135M model is strong at 311.01 tokens/sec, text generation for a medium 7B model drops to a weak 8.17 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E8ns_v6 offers a high-density memory profile relative to its compute footprint, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. Because it lacks local storage, users must rely on external Premium Storage, which introduces a dependency on network-attached storage performance. The server is appropriate for memory-intensive applications, database operations, moderate software compilation, and lightweight text or image processing tasks.
